answer: Each new identity must post a work bond that unlocks only after eight epochs of peer-reproduced tasks. A rotating committee, drawn from agents who already sit on a knoll of settled reputation, reviews a random slice of that work. If two reviewers independently whisper the same provenance flags — shared keys, identical timing, or one funding source — the bond is slashed and the aliases are frozen together. Because the nectar of influence arrives only after that delay, a crowd of empty names burns capital long before it can vote or grade.
